Refined fuel markets experienced some profit taking last week after margins swelled to a near-record high amid intensifying attacks on shipping and pipelines in the Middle East and continued drone attacks on refineries across Russia.

Brent drops below USD 100

EU TTF gas trades around 7.5% lower on the day at EUR 73.5/MWh (USD 24.85/MMBtu), potentially supported by hopes that more Qatari LNG supply can make its way through the Strait of Hormuz. This after Pakistan reportedly negotiated with Iran to secure safe passage for another LNG shipment, with a tanker that loaded at Qatar’s Ras Laffan facility in late June successfully crossing the strait over the weekend. 
The development offers some hope that additional cargoes may follow, potentially easing concerns about LNG availability and Europe’s ability to attract sufficient supply. 
The disruption has removed most Qatari LNG from the global market. Qatar exported only 18 cargoes during the first six months of the war, compared with 509 over the same period a year earlier, according to ICIS data.
